renders._yaml:
- component: advanced_viz
  id: category_bars
  title: Structural categories per sample
  description: |-
    Each bar is a sample, split into the share of its isoforms (or of its FLNC reads, with the level control) in each structural category. It answers how much of a sample's transcriptome matches the reference annotation and how much is novel.
    How to read: a high share of full splice matches means the sample is well covered by the reference. Large novel categories (NIC, NNC) are either real new isoforms or artefacts, so compare the isoform level with the read level: novel isoforms backed by few reads are the first to doubt. Switch the level to see whether the novelty is in many rare isoforms or in a few abundant ones.
    Lines and annotations: the categories follow SQANTI3. FSM is a full splice match to a reference transcript, ISM an incomplete one, NIC a new combination of known splice sites, NNC an isoform with at least one unannotated splice site. Genic intron isoforms sit inside an annotated intron, genic genomic ones overlap introns and exons, antisense ones lie on the opposite strand of a gene and intergenic ones outside any gene.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wiki/ConesaLab/SQANTI3/SQANTI3-isoform-classification:-categories-and-subcategories.md
  kind: stacked_bar
  config:
    default_rank: Isoforms
    value_title: Share of the sample (%)
    x_title: Sample
  roles:
    sample_id: sample
    taxon: structural_category
    rank: level
    abundance: pct

- component: interactive
  title: Isoforms or reads
  description: |-
    Choose whether the shares count isoforms or FLNC reads. It answers whether a category is large because it holds many distinct isoforms or because it holds many reads.
    How to read: select one level at a time. Selecting both stacks two different denominators in the same table.
  interactive_type: MultiSelect
  column_name: level

- component: table
  title: Category composition table
  description: |-
    Each row is a sample, a level (isoforms or reads) and a structural category with its count and its share of that sample and level. It answers the exact numbers behind the bars.
    How to read: sort by share to find the dominant category of each sample, and compare the two levels for the same category.

- component: advanced_viz
  id: gene_isoform_plane
  title: Isoforms against read support per gene
  description: |-
    Each point is a gene in one sample: the full-length reads behind it on the horizontal axis (log scale) and the number of distinct isoforms TAMA found on the vertical axis, coloured by the most common structural category among its isoforms. It answers which genes carry the most isoform diversity and whether that diversity is backed by reads.
    How to read: genes high on the plot have many isoforms. Isoform count rises with read depth, so a gene that sits high at low read support is the more surprising one. A gene with many isoforms that are mostly novel categories is a candidate for follow-up or for artefacts.
  kind: scatter_xy
  config:
    log_x: true
    x_title: FLNC reads supporting the gene
    y_title: Isoforms per gene
    top_n_labels: 10
  roles:
    x: read_support
    y: isoforms
    label: gene_name
    color: top_category

- component: card
  title: Genes with isoforms
  description: |-
    The hero number counts the gene entries (one per sample and gene) with at least one isoform, and the bars split them into annotated and novel genes. The second figure counts the distinct gene ids over all samples. It answers how many genes the long reads reach and how many are not in the reference.
    How to read: a small novel share is expected for a well annotated organism. A large one is worth checking against the reference GTF used for the structural categories.
  column: gene_id
  aggregation: count
  aggregations:
  - nunique
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: gene_status
  top_n_count: 2
  caption: genes, by annotation status
  headline: true

- component: card
  title: Isoforms per gene
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median isoform count per gene and sample, and the box shows its quartiles. It answers how many isoforms a typical gene carries.
    How to read: most genes carry one or two isoforms, and the long upper whisker is the few genes with rich splicing. A rise in the median usually follows deeper sequencing, so compare samples of similar depth.
  column: isoforms
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: isoforms per gene, with their spread

- component: table
  title: Genes table
  description: |-
    Each row is a gene in one sample: the isoform count, the reads behind it, how many isoforms fall in each structural category and the read share of its dominant isoform. It answers which genes to open in the isoform structure view.
    How to read: sort by isoform count, then read the dominant isoform share. A low share means the reads are spread over several isoforms, a high one that one isoform dominates the gene.

- component: advanced_viz
  id: polya_tail_profile
  title: Poly(A) tail length distribution
  description: |-
    Each curve is a sample: the share of its FLNC reads (vertical axis) with each poly(A) tail length removed by TAMA's clean-up (horizontal axis, nucleotides). It answers how long the tails were and whether the samples agree.
    How to read: a pile near 0 nt means TAMA found little tail left to remove, for instance because an earlier step had already clipped it. Curves that differ between samples point to a library preparation difference to check before comparing the samples.
    Lines and annotations: this catalog's recipe pools every tail of 100 nt or longer into the last point, so it is a sum and not a single length. No cut-off is drawn.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wiki/GenomeRIK/tama/Home.md
  kind: profile
  config:
    x_title: Poly(A) tail length removed (nt)
    y_title: Share of the sample's reads (%)
  roles:
    series: sample
    x: tail_length
    y: pct

- component: table
  title: Poly(A) tail table
  description: |-
    Each row is a sample and a tail length with the number of reads and their share of the sample. It answers the exact counts behind each curve.
    How to read: sort by reads to find the modal tail length of each sample.

- component: advanced_viz
  id: isoform_structures
  title: Isoform structures against the reference
  description: |-
    Each lane is a transcript of one gene: boxes are its exons, and the reference transcripts of the gene sit beside the TAMA isoforms of the chosen sample. It answers how an isoform's exon structure differs from the annotation.
    How to read: lanes coloured as full splice matches repeat a reference structure, and novel categories show skipped, extra or shifted exons against the reference lanes. Pick the gene and the sample from the controls, and compare a novel isoform's read support with the reference before trusting it.
    Lines and annotations: the lane colour is the structural category, following SQANTI3 (FSM full splice match, ISM incomplete, NIC new combination of known splice sites, NNC at least one unannotated splice site). Reference lanes are coloured as the reference class.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wiki/ConesaLab/SQANTI3/SQANTI3-isoform-classification:-categories-and-subcategories.md
  kind: transcript_structure
  config:
    colour_by: transcript_class
  roles:
    transcript_id: transcript_id
    gene_id: gene_id
    chrom: chrom
    start: start
    end: end
    feature: feature
    strand: strand
    sample: sample
    gene_name: gene_name
    transcript_class: transcript_class
    expression: expression

- component: table
  title: Exon blocks table
  description: |-
    Each row is an exon or CDS block of a transcript with its coordinates, strand, structural class and read support. It answers the exact coordinates behind the lanes.
    How to read: filter on a gene and compare the blocks of an isoform with the reference rows of the same gene.

outputs.name: Isoforms with read support and structural category

renders._yaml:
- component: advanced_viz
  id: isoform_support_plane
  title: Isoform length against read support
  description: |-
    Each point is an isoform of the merged transcriptome: its spliced length on the horizontal axis and the full-length reads collapsed into it on the vertical axis (log scale), coloured by structural category. It answers which novel isoforms are well supported.
    How to read: novel isoforms (NIC, NNC) high on the plot are the well supported ones worth following up. Novel isoforms at the bottom rest on one or two reads, so treat them with caution: the SQANTI study found that a share of novel long-read isoforms are technical artefacts.
    Lines and annotations: the colours are the structural categories of SQANTI3 (FSM full splice match, ISM incomplete, NIC new combination of known splice sites, NNC at least one unannotated splice site). No cut-off is drawn.
    Sources: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wiki/ConesaLab/SQANTI3/SQANTI3-isoform-classification:-categories-and-subcategories.md and https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29440222/
  kind: scatter_xy
  config:
    log_y: true
    x_title: Isoform length (nt)
    y_title: FLNC reads supporting the isoform
    top_n_labels: 10
  roles:
    x: transcript_length
    y: read_support
    label: transcript_id
    color: structural_category

- component: figure
  title: Isoform length by category
  description: |-
    Each box is a structural category: the spread of isoform lengths in it. It answers whether novel isoforms are shorter or longer than the isoforms that match the reference.
    How to read: incomplete splice matches (ISM) lack 5' exons of their reference transcript, so they can be shorter than full splice matches. A category much shorter than the rest may reflect partial reads. Similar lengths across categories argue for real isoforms.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wiki/ConesaLab/SQANTI3/SQANTI3-isoform-classification:-categories-and-subcategories.md
  visu_type: box
  dict_kwargs:
    x: structural_category
    y: transcript_length
    color: structural_category
    labels:
      structural_category: Structural category
      transcript_length: Isoform length (nt)

- component: card
  title: Isoforms in the merge
  description: |-
    The hero number counts the isoforms of the merged transcriptome, and the bars rank the structural categories by how many isoforms each holds. The second figure counts the distinct isoform ids. It answers how large the transcriptome is and what it is made of.
    How to read: a leading full splice match bar means the data mostly confirm the annotation. A leading novel category means the reference is incomplete for this tissue or the data hold many artefacts.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wiki/ConesaLab/SQANTI3/SQANTI3-isoform-classification:-categories-and-subcategories.md
  column: transcript_id
  aggregation: count
  aggregations:
  - nunique
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: structural_category
  top_n_count: 4
  caption: isoforms, by structural category
  headline: true

- component: card
  title: Read support per isoform
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median count of full-length reads behind an isoform, with the quartiles and the maximum beside it. It answers how well supported a typical isoform is.
    How to read: a median of one or two reads means most isoforms are singletons and the transcriptome is under-sampled. A maximum orders of magnitude above the median is normal, since a few abundant genes dominate the reads.
  column: read_support
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - q1
  - q3
  - max
  secondary_layout: compact
  caption: reads per isoform, median with its quartiles and maximum

- component: interactive
  title: Structural category
  description: |-
    Pick one or more structural categories to restrict every tile of the tab to those isoforms. It answers what the novel isoforms alone look like.
    How to read: select NIC and NNC to look at novel isoforms only, then read the support scatter.
  interactive_type: MultiSelect
  column_name: structural_category

- component: table
  title: Isoforms table
  description: |-
    Each row is an isoform: its position, exon count, length, read support, structural category and the reference gene and transcript it matches. It answers which isoforms to follow up.
    How to read: filter to a novel category and sort by read support to list the best supported new isoforms.
